direction:
The Acceptable Error: understated 1960s bureaucratic retro-futurism in the spirit of Brazil (film), but original. Industrial gray, slate, blue-gray, cream, muted teal and small restrained signal accents. Smooth flat pixel clusters, deliberate economical colors, clean silhouettes, occasional patched panels, screws and fasteners. NO steampunk brass, gears, leather-bound antiques, fantasy devices, heavy grime, decorative rivet overload, noisy dithering, gradient haze, anti-aliasing or text baked into the interface frame. LOCKED SOURCE DIMENSIONS: main scene backgrounds EXACTLY 314×206 logical pixels, displayed at 4× nearest-neighbor; NPC portraits EXACTLY 564×278 pixels, displayed at 1× with independently composited background and foreground layers when applicable; item inventory icons EXACTLY 96×96 pixels on a transparent canvas, displayed at 1× within the approved slot; item inspection illustrations EXACTLY 565×451 pixels, displayed at 1×. These are production dimensions, not suggestions. Never resize a low-resolution scene into a portrait or inspector illustration. Scene-to-portrait environment pairing: where an NPC conversation occurs, author a separate OPAQUE portrait background at exactly 564×278 that depicts the same physical location as its 314×206 main scene, but with a tighter, more detailed and perspective-consistent camera view. Do not resize, crop, blur, or upscale the main scene to produce this background. Each NPC pose is a distinct TRANSPARENT RGBA PNG foreground, exactly 564×278, with fully transparent pixels outside the sprite (no painted environment and no baked-in background). Independently layer the foreground over the matching opaque portrait background; share that background across every pose at the location. Main scene and paired portrait background should maintain coherent architecture, furniture, lighting and palette, without reproducing identical framing. ENVIRONMENTAL TEXT AND SIGNAGE — LEGIBILITY CONTRACT: Maintain the deliberately chunky, economical pixel-cluster style. At 314×206 source resolution, any words intended to be read in the main scene MUST be drawn clearly at that native resolution, before 4× nearest-neighbor presentation; 4× display scaling does not make undersized lettering more legible. Reserve fully readable main-scene text for one or two important focal signs per scene: short, accurately spelled, high-contrast, bold block-capital lettering (prefer 1–3 words where practical), with substantial strokes, open counters and spacing, ideally front-facing or only slightly angled. Large marquees may carry longer titles ONLY when their letters remain unambiguously readable at native resolution. Never generate blurry, anti-aliased, faux-pixelated, misspelled or almost-readable lettering. For directories, notices, forms, tiny labels and distant signs that cannot fit clearly, show convincing NON-LETTER graphic marks, bars, or simple iconography instead of malformed word-like gibberish; do not imply that tiny pseudo-text is actually readable. If a specific message is important but will not fit, shorten the sign, enlarge or recompose it, or supply the exact legible wording in a separate, independently authored 564×278 close portrait background, Focus A close-up, or 565×451 item inspection view as appropriate. Portrait-background text can use finer detail but must still be readable at its own 564×278 source size; never cram in microtype or repurpose a scaled-up main scene. Environmental signage is permitted; do not bake text into the UI frame. All artwork is draft-only unless record status is reused or approved.

EXPOSITION CONTINUITY — OWNER WORKING DIRECTION (2026-11-14): The approved M2 reception main scene is the architectural authority and must remain completely unchanged, including its approved portrait layers. Preserve the existing three-door-bay facade; enter its central bay into an enclosed vestibule, with container chute before the turnstile. Property intake leads through the doors beyond its counter into the reception queue side. The existing right-hand reception double doors lead to the facilities corridor. New interiors share square muted-teal posts/deep rectangular beams, straight lintels, gray wall panels, broad matte gray floor tiles, cream capped service counters/seating, teal mullions, modest steel hardware and compact rectangular fluorescent lights. Preserve distinct functions: enclosed admission control, compact custody workspace, spacious reception with queue and exterior glazing, quieter circulation corridor. Do not make every space another reception desk. No vaulted arcades, mirrored floors, red carpet, detached outdoor gateway or invented courtyard. Keep the Exposition's successful main marquee lettering and the street composition substantially intact.

OPERATIONAL PICTOGRAMS AND NARRATION: Prefer a consistent mid-century institutional family of cream symbols on muted-blue enamel, clear human/rectangle/tray/container silhouettes, common solid arrows and hard pixel edges. The ambiguous facilities cue is a small human beside a plain hollow square, with a real right-hand occluding corner hiding the destination; no roof, toilet, WC, male/female pair or premature exhibit explanation. Use a crossed ordinary box and deposit arrow at the chute, four available shallow trays for custody, and a person at a desk for reception. No operational prose signs or pseudo-text; legible tray numerals 1-4 may remain. Do not invent off-camera written notices or an unseen door plaque to preserve quoted narration. Related prose changes are a separate owner-review proposal; do not silently apply them or change branching/choices/logic. Approved reception artwork remains unchanged; the proposed directions refer directly to its existing right-hand door pair. New artwork candidates remain generated pending visual approval. Final main-scene source files are exactly 314x206; review at that size and at 4x nearest-neighbor in the complete five-scene sequence.

MAIN-SCENE POPULATION — OWNER DIRECTION: Apart from the unchanged owner-approved reception, show no people in scene backgrounds: no attendants, clerks, passersby, silhouettes, human reflections or humanoid stand-ins. Services operate through mundane speaker grilles, intercoms, mechanical trays, indicators and ticket slots. Keep equipment functional and non-anthropomorphic, with no robot faces or limbs. Human-shaped pictograms remain flat wayfinding symbols and are not characters. Preserve the approved receptionist and reception scene completely. Any resulting prose changes remain a separate, reviewable proposal; do not silently change active dialogue, routes, choices or gameplay.

exposition/facilities_corridor.title: AMBIGUOUS FACILITIES HALL
exposition/facilities_corridor.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Finished narrative adventure-game environment art, not a composition diagram, not a mockup. Primary reference is the owner-approved reception image: preserve its 1960s municipal retro-futurist visual family, chunky low-resolution pixel clusters, square muted teal structural frame, medium warm-gray panels, broad MATTE gray floor tiles with restrained dark joints, cream edges and fluorescent fixtures, and plain steel hardware. Deliberate clean edges, economical colors, strong silhouettes, no gradients/haze, no smoothing, no fine noisy textures, no dithering, no photorealism. Author on a 314 by 206 logical pixel grid, native 314x206 PNG if possible. If the service requires a larger transport raster, preserve that exact logical grid/aspect and expose chunky logical pixels; this is low-resolution game art, not detailed concept painting. Fill the frame, no borders, labels, letterboxing or UI. No operational words, no alphabetic lettering, no fake text, no written notices anywhere (including out-of-frame invented notices), no watermark. Symbols are cream on muted-blue enamel and must remain recognizable at the final logical resolution. No brass, gears, mirror floors, vaulted interior arcades, red carpet or ornamental rivet noise. Study/blocking references are COMPOSITION ONLY: render fully finished environment art with original lighting, material shapes and restrained lived-in details comparable to the reception reference; do not output plain flat placeholder diagrams. Never paint over or regenerate the approved reception itself. Provide ONE scene only, no contact sheet.

Facilities corridor candidate. Reference roles: image 1 is approved reception style/material authority; image 2 is the agreed corridor blocking. Camera is just BEYOND reception's existing RIGHT-HAND teal double doors; those doors are BEHIND this camera, not invented again at the far end. A long softly humming institutional corridor in the same square teal post-and-beam system and warm gray paneled walls, broad matte gray floor and rectangular cream fluorescent lights. Keep the FUNCTIONAL character distinct: quieter, narrower circulation space with restrained wall conduits, one internal glazed panel (no outside sky), optional short cream waiting seat matching reception, no service counter or clerk. Show a genuine RIGHT-HAND/EAST turn blocked by a broad structural pier so the destination is physically not yet visible. A blue enamel sign on the visible face BEFORE the turn shows one small cream HUMAN FIGURE BESIDE A PLAIN SQUARE ENCLOSURE; next to it, a matching solid right-pointing arrow. This sign is the humorous ambiguous facilities/comfort pictogram. The human must have a clear head, simple torso and two legs; the square is hollow, plain and unroofed. No male/female pair, literal toilet, WC, house roof or residence/exhibit title. The pier must REALLY OCCLUDE the onward view. No written explanation on an invented off-camera notice. Do not end the corridor at the sign or draw a door inside the square symbol. Continue the walkable floor to the right behind the pier, with further passage implied beyond. No outside/courtyard windows, mirror-reflection floor, red carpet, decorative globe, visible model residence or art gallery. Chunky economical pixel clusters and consistent teal beam proportions; a believable same-building corridor, not an identical reception room. Targeted owner correction: reduce the two-panel facilities sign to fit its actual column faces with clear margins. Keep the human-and-square pictogram on the front face; mount the smaller right-arrow plaque flush to the receding right face, foreshortened toward its right-hand vanishing direction. Preserve all other image pixels.
